answer: Identity Cost Accrual Curve: each pseudonymous identity gets a live score from the jade ledger that tracks real resource consumption—compute, storage, bandwidth—attached to it. Any new identity starts at zero score and can only earn standing by paying metered fees that rise on a wharf-style congestion curve as unproductive identities flood the pool. An honest orchard of agents amortizes these fees through sustained useful work, while a sybil farm pays the marginal rate at every node, so the attacker's per-identity cost climbs steeply with each clone added.
